So is a culture that to this day has failed to keep women safe, in America and everywhere else. 无论最终判决如何，面临审判的不仅是案件被告。在美国及世界各地，那种迄今仍未能保障女性安全的社会文化，同样在接受公众的审视。 A familiar sense of outrage: Why does it feel as if every generation gets its own campus rape story . 一种似曾相识的愤怒： 为什么每一代人似乎 都有校园性侵事件的记忆 ？ 本文节译自时报全球新闻电邮 The World 。 翻译：纽约时报中文网

title: 全球首富的崛起之路：马斯克纪录片讲了些什么
description: MATTHEW HUFF2026年10月13日纪录片里的马斯克。 Bleeker Street Alex Gibney opens his documentary about the tech titan Elon Musk with a question: “How could Musk assume so much power, and why had we given it to him?” 亚历克斯·吉布尼关于科技巨头埃隆·马斯克的纪录片以这样一个问题开场：“马斯克怎么能获得这么大的权力，而我们又为什么把这些权力交给了他？” The Oscar-winning filmmaker, whose previous subjects include Enron and Scientology, spends nearly four hours answering that question in “Musk,” tracing the rise of the Tesla chairman and chief executive from his childhood in South Africa to the I.P.O. of SpaceX in June, which made Musk the world’s first trillionaire. (The movie, in theaters, has a 10-minute intermission baked in.) 这位曾经拍过安然公司和山达基教的奥斯卡获奖导演在《马斯克》一片中用近四个小时的时间来回答这个问题，追溯了这位特斯拉董事长兼首席执行官的崛起之路，从他在南非的童年一直讲到今年6月SpaceX首次公开募股——这让马斯克成为世界上首位身家达到万亿美元的富豪。（这部正在影院上映的电影安排了10分钟的中场休息。） When news of Gibney’s project broke back in 2023, Musk took to Twitter (now X) to preemptively call it a “hit piece.” Combining interviews with ex-wives and former colleagues and clips from Musk’s 30-plus years in the spotlight with commentary from an A.I. version of Musk constructed from an archive of his own words, the film follows his rise from Silicon Valley start-ups to his brief tenure as the de facto head of the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). 2023年，吉布尼正在拍摄这部纪录片的消息传出后，马斯克就在Twitter（现称X）上先发制人，称其为“抹黑之作”。影片采访了马斯克的前妻和前同事，穿插他过去30多年间在公众视野中留下的影像资料，还利用他过去的语音档案建立了一个人工智能版马斯克，让这个虚拟人物对影片内容发表评论。影片记录了马斯克从硅谷创业到短暂担任政府效率部实际负责人的崛起历程。 Here are some takeaways. 以下是影片的几个要点。 影片追溯了这位特斯拉董事长兼首席执行官从南非童年到SpaceX于6月IPO的崛起之路。 Musk’s privileged childhood was marred by violence 马斯克家境优渥的童年笼罩着暴力阴影 “Musk” paints a harrowing portrait of Elon’s youth in apartheid-era South Africa. In one interview, his wealthy businessman father, Errol Musk, claims to have shot and killed three intruders, covering the floor of their home in a “swimming pool” of blood. In another, he describes Elon riding in a car alongside the body of a family friend who had just “dropped dead.” After Elon’s mother, Maye Musk, separated from Errol, claiming physical and mental abuse (charges her former husband has denied), Elon continued to live with his father. When Elon was bullied so badly at school that he was hospitalized for a week, his father, he later said, sided with his attackers. 《马斯克》描绘了埃隆在当时实行种族隔离制度的南非度过的童年岁月，揭示了一段令人不寒而栗的往事。在一次采访中，他的父亲、富商埃罗尔·马斯克声称自己曾开枪打死三名闯入者，鲜血流了一地，在家中地板上积成了一个“游泳池”。在另一次采访中，他描述埃隆坐在一辆车里，旁边是一位刚“猝死”的家族朋友的尸体。埃隆的母亲梅耶·马斯克与埃罗尔分居时，指控丈夫对她实施身体和精神虐待（她的前夫否认了这些指控），但埃隆仍然选择和父亲一起生活。有一次，埃隆在学校遭到严重霸凌，以至于住院一周。据他后来回忆，父亲当时却站在欺负他的那些人一边。 He’s made a habit of failing upward 他屡屡因失败而获利 Gibney suggests that Elon Musk’s business blunders have been as lucrative as his successes. After a failed bid to become the chief executive of his first start-up, Zip2, Musk was pushed out of the company but earned a $22 million buyout. Only a few years later, the entrepreneur and venture capitalist Peter Thiel pushed Musk out of PayPal with a $250 million parting gift. 吉布尼认为，埃隆·马斯克在商业上的失误给他带来的财富并不亚于成功为他带来的财富。他曾试图成为自己创办的第一家初创企业Zip2的首席执行官，但未能如愿，随后被赶出公司，却拿到了2200万美元的收购所得。仅仅几年后，企业家兼风险投资人彼得·蒂尔又将马斯克赶出了贝宝，而马斯克离开时获得了2.5亿美元。 More recently, according to Gibney, Twitter (now X) lost 80 percent of its value after Musk purchased it (though other estimates vary). Musk then rolled X and his A.I. start-up xAI into SpaceX for the largest I.P.O. on record to date, prompting Gibney to ask, “How can you keep screwing up and still make millions?” 吉布尼称，更近的例子是，Twitter（现X）在马斯克收购后损失了80%的价值（不过，不同机构的估算并不一致）。马斯克随后将X和他的AI初创公司xAI并入SpaceX，完成了有记录以来最大的IPO，这让吉布尼不禁发问：“你怎么能一次又一次把事情搞砸，却依然赚得盆满钵满？” Tesla is a lesson in entrepreneurial sleight of hand 特斯拉背后的商业障眼法 While Musk claims to be a founder of Tesla, the automotive company was actually started by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning in 2003. However, Musk negotiated the title of co-founder for himself as part of a 2009 legal settlement. Later, he claimed that Tesla drivers could easily swap out their 1,000-pound car batteries, which helped him garner more than $100 million worth of environmental credits from the state of California, though he had only built a single battery swap facility in the desert. 虽然马斯克自称是特斯拉的创始人，但这家汽车公司实际上由马丁·艾伯哈德和马克·塔彭宁于2003年创立。不过，在2009年达成的一项法律和解协议中，马斯克通过谈判为自己争取到了联合创始人的头衔。后来，他又宣称，特斯拉车主可以轻松更换重达450公斤的汽车电池，这帮助他从加利福尼亚州获得了价值超过1亿美元的环保积分，尽管他仅在沙漠里建了一个电池更换站。 Gibney also dedicates substantial time to Tesla’s self-driving Autopilot feature, which has been linked to deaths and injuries. In 2016, Musk oversaw the creation of a promotional video depicting a self-driving Tesla, causing the company’s stock to rise. However, it was later revealed that humans had controlled the car at certain points during filming and that the car had actually crashed. 吉布尼还用了相当长的篇幅讨论特斯拉的自动驾驶Autopilot系统，该系统被指与多起造成人员伤亡的事故有关。2016年，马斯克主导制作了一段展示特斯拉汽车自动驾驶的宣传视频，推动了公司股价上涨。然而，后来有消息披露，拍摄过程中，汽车在某些时刻实际上由人控制，而且那辆车还发生了撞车事故。 按照吉布尼在片中的说法，马斯克通过星链巩固了自己的政治权力。星链是SpaceX的卫星部门，从太空提供互联网接入。 He sees increasing the birthrate as a “national emergency” 他把提高出生率视为“国家紧急事务” “Musk” includes extended interviews with Justine Musk, Elon’s first wife, and Ashley St. Clair, a former conservative influencer who dated Elon from 2023 to 2025 and gave birth to one of his 14 known children. St. Clair claims to have received messages from multiple women on social media whom Musk offered to impregnate. “It’s like a Gatling gun of sperm in his DMs,” she says in one of the documentary’s more evocative lines. 《马斯克》对埃隆的第一任妻子贾斯廷·马斯克以及曾经的保守派网红阿什莉·圣克莱尔进行了长时间采访。圣克莱尔在2023年至2025年间与埃隆交往，并为他生下一个孩子（马斯克为公众所知的孩子共有14个）。圣克莱尔称，她在社交媒体上收到多名女性发来的私信，她们都说马斯克曾提出要让她们怀孕。她在纪录片中用了一句格外生动的比喻：“他在私信里到处播种，简直就像一挺喷射精子的加特林机枪。” Despite Musk’s preoccupation with procreating, both women suggest that Musk sustains little interest in his children or their mothers. Justine remembers Elon telling her, “I am the alpha in this relationship” at their wedding reception, and later telling her, “If you were my employee, I’d fire you.” St. Clair claims Musk openly called X Æ A-Xii (whose mother is Musk’s former partner Claire Boucher, the musician known as Grimes) his favorite and didn’t care to spend time with his other offspring. 尽管马斯克对生育如此执着，但这两名女性都表示，他对自己的孩子及孩子的母亲几乎没有持续的关心。贾斯廷回忆说，埃隆曾在两人的婚宴上对她说：“在这段关系里，我是老大。”后来又对她说：“如果你是我的员工，我早就把你开除了。”圣克莱尔则称，马斯克曾公开表示，X Æ A-Xii（其母是马斯克之前的伴侣、音乐人格莱姆斯，本名克莱尔·布歇）是他最喜欢的孩子，她还说他不怎么愿意花时间陪伴其他子女。 Starlink and DOGE gave him global reach 星链和政府效率部让他的影响力遍及全球 According to Gibney, Musk has been able to consolidate political power via Starlink, the satellite arm of SpaceX, which provides internet access from space. While Musk supplied Ukrainian forces with necessary tech during their war with Russia, he’s also able to control and withhold access to it. That military bargaining chip has given Musk remarkable leverage in lucrative business deals around the world. 据吉布尼说，马斯克得以通过星链巩固政治权力。星链是SpaceX的卫星部门，从太空提供互联网接入。虽然马斯克在俄乌战争中向乌克兰军队提供了必要的技术，但他同样能够控制甚至切断对这项技术的使用。这一军事筹码让马斯克在全球利润丰厚的商业交易中拥有了非同寻常的议价能力。 As part of his work with DOGE, Musk dispatched gatekeepers and regulations designed to check the A.I. industry. With those barriers removed, Gibney speculates that Musk could use A.I. to amass even more power. 在政府效率部任职期间，马斯克清除了旨在约束人工智能行业的监管把关机制和规定。吉布尼推测，随着这些障碍被移除，马斯克可能利用人工智能进一步扩大自己的权力。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

Justine remembers Elon telling her, “I am the alpha in this relationship” at their wedding reception, and later telling her, “If you were my employee, I’d fire you.” St. Clair claims Musk openly called X Æ A-Xii (whose mother is Musk’s former partner Claire Boucher, the musician known as Grimes ) his favorite and didn’t care to spend time with his other offspring. 尽管马斯克 对生育如此执着 ，但这两名女性都表示，他对自己的孩子及孩子的母亲几乎没有持续的关心。贾斯廷回忆说，埃隆曾在两人的婚宴上对她说：“在这段关系里，我是老大。”后来又对她说：“如果你是我的员工，我早就把你开除了。”圣克莱尔则称，马斯克曾公开表示，X Æ A-Xii（其母是马斯克之前的伴侣、音乐人 格莱姆斯 ，本名克莱尔·布歇）是他最喜欢的孩子，她还说他不怎么愿意花时间陪伴其他子女。 Starlink and DOGE gave him global reach 星链和政府效率部让他的影响力遍及全球 According to Gibney, Musk has been able to consolidate political power via Starlink, the satellite arm of SpaceX, which provides internet access from space. While Musk supplied Ukrainian forces with necessary tech during their war with Russia, he’s also able to control and withhold access to it . That military bargaining chip has given Musk remarkable leverage in lucrative business deals around the world. 据吉布尼说，马斯克得以通过星链巩固政治权力。星链是SpaceX的卫星部门，从太空提供互联网接入。虽然马斯克在俄乌战争中向乌克兰军队提供了必要的技术，但他同样能够 控制甚至切断 对这项技术的使用。这一军事筹码让马斯克在全球利润丰厚的商业交易中拥有了非同寻常的议价能力。 As part of his work with DOGE , Musk dispatched gatekeepers and regulations designed to check the A.I. industry. With those barriers removed, Gibney speculates that Musk could use A.I. to amass even more power. 在政府效率部任职期间 ，马斯克清除了旨在约束人工智能行业的监管把关机制和规定。吉布尼推测，随着这些障碍被移除，马斯克可能利用人工智能进一步扩大自己的权力。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 欧洲为何对中国电动汽车爱恨交加
description: JAMES PATON2026年10月13日位于英国利兹的一家比亚迪展厅。在欧洲售出的汽车中，大约每10辆就有一辆是中国汽车。 Owen Richards for The New York Times BYD, China’s dominant maker of electric vehicles, aims to open so many outlets in Germany that no one has to travel more than 20 minutes to buy one of its cars. One of its Chinese rivals, Xiaomi, sees Germany as the foundation of its European expansion plans, after selling 700,000 cars back home. 中国领先的电动汽车制造商比亚迪计划在德国开设大量销售网点，使任何人前往最近的比亚迪门店买车，路上用时都不超过20分钟。其中国竞争对手之一小米在中国本土售出70万辆汽车后，将德国视为其欧洲扩张计划的基础。 Germany is the birthplace of the automobile and the home of Volkswagen, BMW and Mercedes-Benz. These days, it is also a top destination for Chinese companies selling cars at a considerable discount to European vehicles. 德国是汽车的诞生地，也是大众、宝马和梅赛德斯-奔驰的故乡。如今，这里也已成为中国车企的首选市场，中国车的售价比欧洲车低得多。 “Customers don’t care if it’s a Chinese car or a German car,” said Ferdinand Dudenhöffer, a German auto analyst and former executive at Porsche and other companies. What they do care about, he said, is the price. “顾客不在乎它是中国车还是德国车，”德国汽车分析师、曾在保时捷等公司担任高管的费迪南德·杜登赫费尔说。他说，他们真正在乎的是价格。 Shut out of the United States by tariffs, Chinese automakers have focused on other overseas markets — and Europe is a prime target. Low-cost Chinese car brands are enticing customers across the continent as surging gasoline prices drive interest in electric vehicles. Chinese cars account for about one in every 10 cars sold in Europe, up from one in 100 five years ago. 由于被关税挡在美国之外，中国汽车制造商专注于其他海外市场——欧洲正是主要目标。随着汽油价格飙升，人们对电动汽车的兴趣日益浓厚，低价中国汽车品牌正在吸引整个欧洲大陆的消费者。目前欧洲每售出10辆汽车中就有一辆是中国品牌，而五年前这一比例仅为百分之一。 Chinese brands are rapidly gaining ground on leaders like Volkswagen. BYD’s sales in Europe have more than doubled this year. Sales of another popular Chinese manufacturer, Chery, have grown even faster. The company’s Jaecoo 7, known as the “Temu Range Rover” in a nod to the Chinese bargain-shopping app, was Britain’s best-selling vehicle in September. Xiaomi plans to add to the competition after teaming up with eight dealers in Germany. 中国品牌正在迅速追赶大众等领先品牌。比亚迪今年在欧洲的销量增长了一倍多。另一家受欢迎的中国制造商奇瑞的销量增长更快。该公司的杰酷7是英国9月份最畅销的车型。这款车也被称为“Temu版路虎揽胜”，借用了中国廉价购物应用Temu的名字。小米在与德国八家经销商合作后，计划加入竞争。 中国汽车制造商奇瑞生产的杰酷7上个月成为英国最畅销的车型。 It’s a love-hate relationship, however. Consumers increasingly want to buy Chinese cars. Policymakers are trying to stem the flow. The European Union reached a deal with Beijing on Friday that European officials said could halve the number of hybrid gasoline-electric cars that China sends to the bloc in the next four years. 然而，这是一种爱恨交加的关系。消费者越来越希望购买中国汽车。而政策制定者正试图阻止这股潮流。欧盟周五与北京达成一项协议，欧洲官员称，该协议可能使中国在未来四年向欧盟出口的油电混合动力汽车数量减半。 The agreement could help ease the pain for European carmakers, though much about implementation remains unclear. Cheaper imports from China are threatening the industry, which contributes about 7 percent of the E.U.’s economic output. The E.U. industry chief, Stéphane Séjourné, has warned that the sector is in “mortal danger.” Germany’s auto industry group has predicted the loss of up to 225,000 jobs by 2035. 尽管具体实施细节尚不明确，但该协议或有助于缓解欧洲汽车制造商的困境。来自中国的廉价进口车正威胁该行业，该行业贡献了欧盟约7%的经济产出。欧盟工业主管斯特凡纳·塞茹尔内警告说，该行业正处于“致命危险”之中。德国汽车工业协会预测，到2035年将有多达22.5万个工作岗位流失。 The E.U. has faced growing pressure to impose tougher measures to shield industries from what companies see as unfair competition. Left unchecked, Chinese carmakers could triple their share of the European auto market to as much as 30 percent by 2035, said Harald Hendrikse, a managing director at Citi Research. 欧盟面临越来越大的压力，要求其采取更严厉措施，保护产业免受企业视为不公平竞争的影响。花旗研究董事总经理哈拉尔德·亨德里克塞说，如果放任不管，到2035年，中国汽车制造商在欧洲汽车市场的份额可能增加两倍，达到30%。 In taking on China, Europe faces a conundrum: How can the region protect its industries while keeping prices affordable? Efforts to insulate the sector would come with a cost. 在与中国的较量中，欧洲面临一个难题：该地区如何在保护其产业的同时保持价格可负担？保护该行业的努力将伴随成本。 “There’s no free lunch in protectionism,” said David Bailey, a professor and industrial policy expert at University of Birmingham. “European and British automakers may gain some breathing room, but consumers could face higher prices and less choice, especially at the lower end of the market.” “保护主义中没有免费的午餐，”伯明翰大学工业政策专家、教授戴维·贝利说。“欧洲和英国汽车制造商可能获得一些喘息空间，但消费者可能面临更高价格和更少选择，尤其是在低端市场。” For example, one proposal being considered would steer public spending toward European companies, prioritizing battery cells made in the region. But such a rule could raise the price of an electric car by 2,100 euros, or more than $2,300, according to researchers at Bruegel, a think tank in Brussels. 例如，正在考虑的一项提案将把公共支出引向欧洲公司，优先使用该地区制造的电池电芯。但布鲁塞尔智库布鲁盖尔的研究人员称，这样的规定可能使一辆电动汽车的价格提高2100欧元。 “Who will potentially lose from all of this?” asked Simone Tagliapietra, a deputy director at Bruegel. “I would say the middle class. They need to buy cars, right? And pushing up the cost with such provisions might be costly and even prevent them from accessing technology that, given the current energy crisis, is existentially important for Europeans.” “这一切最终可能让谁蒙受损失？”布鲁盖尔副主管西蒙娜·塔利亚皮耶特拉问道。“我会说是中产阶级。他们需要买车，对吧？而此类条款带来的推高成本可能代价高昂，甚至可能使他们无法获得这项技术——鉴于当前的能源危机，这项技术对欧洲人至关重要。” In 2024, the European Union imposed tariffs as high as 45 percent on Chinese electric cars to try to counter Beijing’s subsidies. But the bloc spared hybrid vehicles, which were then still a small segment of the market. Chinese manufacturers pivoted, boosting exports of hybrids, which are subject to only a 10 percent tariff. 2024年，欧盟对中国电动汽车征收高达45%的关税，试图抵消北京补贴的影响。但欧盟对混合动力汽车予以豁免，当时该车型在市场上仍仅占很小份额。中国制造商随即调整策略，增加混合动力汽车出口，而这类车仅适用10%的关税。 Chinese hybrids have since poured into Europe, accounting for more than a fifth of the category’s total sales and pushing policymakers to consider wider trade restrictions. In Poland, Hungary and Romania, Chinese companies have gained more than half of the plug-in hybrid market, according to Dataforce, which tracks the auto sector. 此后，中国混合动力汽车涌入欧洲，占该类别总销量的五分之一以上，促使政策制定者考虑更广泛的贸易限制。根据追踪汽车行业的Dataforce的数据，在波兰、匈牙利和罗马尼亚，中国公司已获得插电式混合动力市场一半以上的份额。 History shows restricting supplies of those Chinese cars would probably increase prices, which over time could benefit the country’s manufacturers in Europe. In 2013, China agreed to reduce the number of solar panels that it shipped to Europe. In turn, Chinese manufacturers raised prices, pulling in larger profits that they could invest in research and new factories. 历史表明，限制这些中国汽车的供应可能会推高价格，而从长远来看，这反而可能使中国汽车制造商在欧洲获益。2013年，中国同意减少向欧洲出口的太阳能电池板数量。作为回应，中国制造商提高了价格，从而获得了更高的利润，并可将这些利润用于投资研发和新工厂建设。 Today China dominates the world’s solar industry. 如今，中国主导着全球太阳能产业。 Chinese companies have their eye on the long term, seeing this period as a “bridge” toward making cars on European soil, said Matthias Schmidt, an industry analyst in Germany. He pointed to Leapmotor’s production partnership with Stellantis and BYD’s plan to produce cars in Hungary. 德国行业分析师马蒂亚斯·施密特说，中国公司着眼于长期，将这一时期视为迈向在欧洲本土生产汽车的“桥梁”。他提到零跑汽车与斯泰兰蒂斯的生产合作，以及比亚迪在匈牙利生产汽车的计划。 像奇瑞这样的中国企业仍然认为欧洲市场蕴藏着巨大的机遇，即使新的贸易措施会放缓它们在欧洲的扩张步伐。 Chinese companies still see significant opportunity in Europe, even if new trade measures slow their advance. Spain is among the countries where they have seen strong demand and taken advantage of an increasing appetite for electric and hybrid vehicles. Electric cars have caught up with gas-powered vehicles, and electrics and hybrids together make up more than two thirds of the European market. 尽管新的贸易措施放缓了中国企业的扩张步伐，但它们仍认为欧洲市场蕴藏着巨大机遇。西班牙便是其中之一：中国公司在那里发现了强劲需求，抓住了当地人对电动车和混动车越来越感兴趣的机会。电动汽车的销量已追平燃油车，而电动汽车和混合动力车合计占据了欧洲市场三分之二以上的份额。 At the end of last year, Spain had about 600 dealerships selling Chinese brands. By the end of 2026, that number will likely grow to 1,000, according to Faconauto, a dealership association in Madrid. The market share of Chinese brands in Spain has risen fivefold in three years to about 15 percent, led by BYD and MG, the iconic British automaker now owned by a Chinese state-run company. 去年年底，西班牙约有600家销售中国品牌的经销商。根据马德里经销商协会Faconauto的预测，到2026年底，这一数字可能增长到1000家。在比亚迪和名爵带动下，中国品牌在西班牙的市场份额三年内增至五倍，达到约15%，名爵是标志性的英国汽车制造商，现为中国国有企业所有。 “For the Spanish people, this is very good,” said Marta Blázquez, Faconauto’s president. “这对西班牙人来说是好事，”Faconauto总裁玛尔塔·布拉斯克斯说。 Chinese brands have retained a significant edge on price compared with their European peers, though the gap has narrowed from a discount of as much as 30 percent in recent years, she said. The Center for European Policy Analysis in February estimated that the average starting price for a BYD electric vehicle in Europe ranged from €30,000 to €45,000, compared with prices closer to €50,000 for European E.V.s. 她说，与欧洲同行相比，中国品牌在价格上保持了显著优势，但这一差距已从近年高达30%的折扣幅度有所收窄。欧洲政策分析中心2月估计，比亚迪电动汽车在欧洲的平均起售价在3万至4.5万欧元之间，而欧洲电动汽车的价格接近5万欧元。 In Germany, even though Chinese car brands remain smaller players, they’re growing quickly. BYD said it planned to expand to as many as 300 dealerships by the end of the year. After more than doubling in 2025, sales of Chinese cars in Germany have continued to surge this year, according to Inovev, a consulting firm in Paris. 在德国，尽管中国汽车品牌仍是较小的参与者，但它们增长迅速。计划在今年年底前将经销商网络扩展至多达300家。根据巴黎咨询公司Inovev的数据，中国汽车在德国的销量在2025年增长一倍多后，今年继续激增。 Stefan Bratzel, director of the Center of Automotive Management in Germany, invoked Frank Sinatra in explaining the importance of the country for Chinese car companies. The way they see it, “if you can make it there, you can make it anywhere.” 德国汽车管理中心主任斯特凡·布拉策尔在解释德国对中国汽车公司的重要性时引用了弗兰克·辛纳屈的歌词——在他们看来，“如果你能在那里成功，就能在任何地方成功。” James Paton是《纽约时报》国际商业与经济记者，常驻伦敦。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

The E.U. industry chief, Stéphane Séjourné, has warned that the sector is in “mortal danger.” Germany’s auto industry group has predicted the loss of up to 225,000 jobs by 2035. 尽管具体实施细节尚不明确，但该协议或有助于缓解欧洲汽车制造商的困境。来自中国的廉价进口车正威胁该行业，该行业贡献了欧盟约7%的经济产出。欧盟工业主管斯特凡纳·塞茹尔内警告说，该行业正处于“致命危险”之中。德国汽车工业协会预测，到2035年将有多达22.5万个工作岗位流失。 The E.U. has faced growing pressure to impose tougher measures to shield industries from what companies see as unfair competition. Left unchecked, Chinese carmakers could triple their share of the European auto market to as much as 30 percent by 2035, said Harald Hendrikse, a managing director at Citi Research. 欧盟面临越来越大的压力，要求其采取更严厉措施，保护产业免受企业视为不公平竞争的影响。花旗研究董事总经理哈拉尔德·亨德里克塞说，如果放任不管，到2035年，中国汽车制造商在欧洲汽车市场的份额可能增加两倍，达到30%。 In taking on China, Europe faces a conundrum: How can the region protect its industries while keeping prices affordable? Efforts to insulate the sector would come with a cost. 在与中国的较量中，欧洲面临一个难题：该地区如何在保护其产业的同时保持价格可负担？保护该行业的努力将伴随成本。 “There’s no free lunch in protectionism,” said David Bailey, a professor and industrial policy expert at University of Birmingham. “European and British automakers may gain some breathing room, but consumers could face higher prices and less choice, especially at the lower end of the market.” “保护主义中没有免费的午餐，”伯明翰大学工业政策专家、教授戴维·贝利说。“欧洲和英国汽车制造商可能获得一些喘息空间，但消费者可能面临更高价格和更少选择，尤其是在低端市场。” For example, one proposal being considered would steer public spending toward European companies, prioritizing battery cells made in the region. But such a rule could raise the price of an electric car by 2,100 euros, or more than $2,300, according to researchers at Bruegel , a think tank in Brussels. 例如，正在考虑的一项提案将把公共支出引向欧洲公司，优先使用该地区制造的电池电芯。但布鲁塞尔智库 布鲁盖尔 的研究人员称，这样的规定可能使一辆电动汽车的价格提高2100欧元。 “Who will potentially lose from all of this?” asked Simone Tagliapietra, a deputy director at Bruegel. “I would say the middle class. They need to buy cars, right? And pushing up the cost with such provisions might be costly and even prevent them from accessing technology that, given the current energy crisis, is existentially important for Europeans.” “这一切最终可能让谁蒙受损失？”布鲁盖尔副主管西蒙娜·塔利亚皮耶特拉问道。“我会说是中产阶级。他们需要买车，对吧？而此类条款带来的推高成本可能代价高昂，甚至可能使他们无法获得这项技术——鉴于当前的能源危机，这项技术对欧洲人至关重要。” In 2024, the European Union imposed tariffs as high as 45 percent on Chinese electric cars to try to counter Beijing’s subsidies. But the bloc spared hybrid vehicles, which were then still a small segment of the market. Chinese manufacturers pivoted, boosting exports of hybrids, which are subject to only a 10 percent tariff. 2024年，欧盟对中国电动汽车征收高达45%的关税，试图抵消北京补贴的影响。但欧盟对混合动力汽车予以豁免，当时该车型在市场上仍仅占很小份额。中国制造商随即调整策略，增加混合动力汽车出口，而这类车仅适用10%的关税。 Chinese hybrids have since poured into Europe, accounting for more than a fifth of the category’s total sales and pushing policymakers to consider wider trade restrictions. In Poland, Hungary and Romania, Chinese companies have gained more than half of the plug-in hybrid market, according to Dataforce, which tracks the auto sector. 此后，中国混合动力汽车涌入欧洲，占该类别总销量的五分之一以上，促使政策制定者考虑更广泛的贸易限制。根据追踪汽车行业的Dataforce的数据，在波兰、匈牙利和罗马尼亚，中国公司已获得插电式混合动力市场一半以上的份额。 History shows restricting supplies of those Chinese cars would probably increase prices, which over time could benefit the country’s manufacturers in Europe. In 2013, China agreed to reduce the number of solar panels that it shipped to Europe. In turn, Chinese manufacturers raised prices, pulling in larger profits that they could invest in research and new factories. 历史表明，限制这些中国汽车的供应可能会推高价格，而从长远来看，这反而可能使中国汽车制造商在欧洲获益。2013年，中国同意减少向欧洲出口的太阳能电池板数量。作为回应，中国制造商提高了价格，从而获得了更高的利润，并可将这些利润用于投资研发和新工厂建设。 Today China dominates the world’s solar industry. 如今，中国主导着全球太阳能产业。 Chinese companies have their eye on the long term, seeing this period as a “bridge” toward making cars on European soil, said Matthias Schmidt, an industry analyst in Germany. He pointed to Leapmotor’s production partnership with Stellantis and BYD’s plan to produce cars in Hungary. 德国行业分析师马蒂亚斯·施密特说，中国公司着眼于长期，将这一时期视为迈向在欧洲本土生产汽车的“桥梁”。他提到零跑汽车与斯泰兰蒂斯的生产合作，以及比亚迪在匈牙利生产汽车的计划。 像奇瑞这样的中国企业仍然认为欧洲市场蕴藏着巨大的机遇，即使新的贸易措施会放缓它们在欧洲的扩张步伐。 Chinese companies still see significant opportunity in Europe, even if new trade measures slow their advance. Spain is among the countries where they have seen strong demand and taken advantage of an increasing appetite for electric and hybrid vehicles. Electric cars have caught up with gas-powered vehicles, and electrics and hybrids together make up more than two thirds of the European market. 尽管新的贸易措施放缓了中国企业的扩张步伐，但它们仍认为欧洲市场蕴藏着巨大机遇。西班牙便是其中之一：中国公司在那里发现了强劲需求，抓住了当地人对电动车和混动车越来越感兴趣的机会。电动汽车的销量已追平燃油车，而电动汽车和混合动力车合计占据了欧洲市场三分之二以上的份额。 At the end of last year, Spain had about 600 dealerships selling Chinese brands. By the end of 2026, that number will likely grow to 1,000, according to Faconauto, a dealership association in Madrid. The market share of Chinese brands in Spain has risen fivefold in three years to about 15 percent, led by BYD and MG, the iconic British automaker now owned by a Chinese state-run company. 去年年底，西班牙约有600家销售中国品牌的经销商。根据马德里经销商协会Faconauto的预测，到2026年底，这一数字可能增长到1000家。在比亚迪和名爵带动下，中国品牌在西班牙的市场份额三年内增至五倍，达到约15%，名爵是标志性的英国汽车制造商，现为中国国有企业所有。 “For the Spanish people, this is very good,” said Marta Blázquez, Faconauto’s president. “这对西班牙人来说是好事，”Faconauto总裁玛尔塔·布拉斯克斯说。 Chinese brands have retained a significant edge on price compared with their European peers, though the gap has narrowed from a discount of as much as 30 percent in recent years, she said. The Center for European Policy Analysis in February estimated that the average starting price for a BYD electric vehicle in Europe ranged from €30,000 to €45,000, compared with prices closer to €50,000 for European E.V.s. 她说，与欧洲同行相比，中国品牌在价格上保持了显著优势，但这一差距已从近年高达30%的折扣幅度有所收窄。欧洲政策分析中心2月估计，比亚迪电动汽车在欧洲的平均起售价在3万至4.5万欧元之间，而欧洲电动汽车的价格接近5万欧元。 In Germany, even though Chinese car brands remain smaller players, they’re growing quickly. BYD said it planned to expand to as many as 300 dealerships by the end of the year. After more than doubling in 2025, sales of Chinese cars in Germany have continued to surge this year, according to Inovev, a consulting firm in Paris. 在德国，尽管中国汽车品牌仍是较小的参与者，但它们增长迅速。计划在今年年底前将经销商网络扩展至多达300家。根据巴黎咨询公司Inovev的数据，中国汽车在德国的销量在2025年增长一倍多后，今年继续激增。 Stefan Bratzel, director of the Center of Automotive Management in Germany, invoked Frank Sinatra in explaining the importance of the country for Chinese car companies. The way they see it, “if you can make it there, you can make it anywhere.” 德国汽车管理中心主任斯特凡·布拉策尔在解释德国对中国汽车公司的重要性时引用了弗兰克·辛纳屈的歌词——在他们看来，“如果你能在那里成功，就能在任何地方成功。” James Paton 是《纽约时报》国际商业与经济记者，常驻伦敦。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 美国研发新型太阳能电池板，或挑战中国垄断地位
description: IVAN PENN2026年10月13日 Producers of solar panels in the United States say they are on the cusp of a technological breakthrough that could upend the industry and even threaten China’s grip on it. 美国太阳能板生产商表示，他们即将迎来一项技术突破，这项突破可能颠覆整个行业，甚至威胁到中国在该行业的垄断地位。 The manufacturers are racing to develop new kinds of panels that can generate 25 percent more energy than most such devices available today. If they are successful, the advance will allow the world to meet the rapidly rising demand for electricity with less land and roof area. 这些制造商正在竞相开发新型太阳能板，其发电量比目前市面上大多数同类产品高出25%。如果成功，这一进步将使世界能以更少的土地和屋顶面积来满足迅速增长的电力需求。 The new technology, known as tandem solar, involves adding second and third layers of material, like a layer cake, to allow panels to convert more of the sun’s radiance into electricity. 这项新技术被称为叠层太阳能，通过像层层蛋糕一样添加第二层和第三层材料，使太阳能电池板能够将更多的太阳辐射转化为电能。 Researchers have been working to perfect tandem panels for many years, but now several companies, including Tandem PV, First Solar and Hanwha Qcells, say they are preparing to sell such panels commercially soon, after successfully testing the devices and obtaining certifications from technical bodies. 研究人员多年来一直致力于完善叠层太阳能电池板，但现在，包括Tandem PV、First Solar和韩华Qcells在内的几家公司表示，在成功测试这些设备并获得技术机构认证后，他们正准备很快将此类电池板投入商业销售。 “It is the next frontier,” said Mike Carr, executive director of the Solar Energy Manufacturers for America Coalition. He acknowledged that Chinese companies were also working on tandem solar but said their technology “is not better than ours and maybe even behind us.” “这是下一个前沿领域，”美国太阳能制造商联盟执行主任迈克·卡尔说。他承认中国企业也在研发叠层太阳能，但表示中国的技术“不比我们的更好，甚至可能落后于我们”。 But the new tandem panels and their manufacturers will face many challenges. Power producers will be reluctant to buy new devices that are too expensive or until manufacturers can convince them that tandem panels will not degrade more quickly than conventional panels. 但新的叠层太阳能板及其制造商将面临许多挑战。电力生产商将不愿购买过于昂贵的新设备，除非制造商能让他们相信，叠层太阳能电池的性能衰减速度不会比传统太阳能电池更快。 U.S. politics could be another barrier. Republicans in Congress and the Trump administration have made it hard for new solar farms to obtain federal permits while trying to increase the use of fossil fuels and nuclear power plants. 美国政治可能是另一个障碍。国会共和党人和特朗普政府一方面试图增加化石燃料和核电站的使用，一方面让新的太阳能发电场难以获得联邦许可。 Then there is China, which controls about 80 percent of the solar panel market by supplying either panels or their components. 此外还有中国，它通过供应太阳能板及其组件控制着约80%的太阳能板市场。 China devastated the U.S. solar panel manufacturing industry by offering devices at prices far lower than companies in the United States, Germany and Japan — which dominated the industry until around 2010. 中国以远低于美国、德国和日本公司的价格提供设备，重创了美国太阳能板制造业；此前，美国、德国和日本曾主导该行业直至2010年左右。 The Biden and Trump administrations have tried to revive U.S. solar manufacturing with tariffs, subsidies and other policies. Partly as a result, new factories have been built across the country in recent years. Hanwha, a South Korean company that bought the German solar manufacturer Qcells in 2012, has spent billions on production lines in Georgia, including in Cartersville, north of Atlanta. 拜登和特朗普政府都试图通过关税、补贴和其他政策重振美国太阳能制造业。部分得益于此，近年来美国各地纷纷建起了新工厂。韩国企业韩华在2012年收购了德国太阳能制造商 Qcells，已在佐治亚州的生产线上投入数十亿美元，包括亚特兰大以北的卡特斯维尔。 Energy experts say perfecting tandem panels before the Chinese do would allow the United States, Germany and other countries to reclaim a big share of the global solar industry. 能源专家表示，若能在中国之前完善叠层电池技术，美国、德国及其他国家将有望重新夺回全球太阳能产业的巨大份额。 Qcells has been testing its tandem solar panels in its lab in Germany as well as in fields in the United States, Australia, Cyprus and South Korea to show that they are ready. Among other things, the company has been blasting panels with LED light to see how they will perform. It has also been firing balls of ice — some roughly the size of marbles, others as big as or slightly bigger than golf balls — at panels to see how they handle extreme weather. Qcells一直在其德国实验室以及美国、澳大利亚、塞浦路斯和韩国的实地测试其叠层太阳能电池板，以证明它们已经准备就绪。除其他测试外，该公司一直用 LED 光照射太阳能电池板，以观察其表现。它还向太阳能电池板发射冰丸——有些大约弹珠大小，另一些与高尔夫球一样大或略大——以检验其应对极端天气的能力。。 Qcells公司进行的一项测试中模拟了冰雹。 The tests are designed to reassure energy companies, investors and lenders that the new panels will last 20 to 30 years once they are installed in baking deserts or in fields subject to torrential downpours. 这些测试旨在让能源公司、投资者和贷款方放心：无论安装在酷热的沙漠中，还是在常受暴雨侵袭的田野里，这些新的太阳能电池板都能使用20至30年。 The power industry is “quite conservative in accepting new technologies,” said Fabian Fertig, head of tandem research and development for Qcells, who is based in Leipzig, Germany. “We’ve been focused on stability. We have to convince banks that this new technology can deliver.” 电力行业“在接受新技术方面相当保守”，Qcells叠层研发负责人法比安·费尔蒂希说。他常驻德国莱比锡。“我们一直专注于稳定性。我们必须让银行相信，这项新技术能够兑现承诺。” Scientists developed early tandem panels decades ago, but it has taken time to ensure that they could withstand harsh conditions — from heat and humidity to pounding hail. 科学家早在几十年前就开发出了早期叠层太阳能电池板，但要确保它们能够承受从高温、高湿到猛烈冰雹等各种恶劣条件，仍花费了相当长的时间。 “There are all these questions around how long they actually last,” said Chetan Krishna, a principal at RMI, a research organization that specializes in sustainability and was previously known as the Rocky Mountain Institute. “Are there degradation issues that we don’t know yet?” “围绕它们实际能用多久存在各种各样的问题，”RMI（一家专注于可持续发展的研究机构，前身为落基山研究所）负责人切坦·克里希纳说。“是否存在我们尚不知道的衰减问题？” Mr. Krishna and other experts say they believe the tandem solar panels are very close to being ready. 克里希纳和其他专家表示，他们认为叠层太阳能电池板已非常接近投入实际应用。 But the technology remains expensive. By some estimates, these panels could cost three to three and a half times as much as conventional devices, which are typically made of one layer of silicon. 但这项技术仍然昂贵。根据一些估计，这些太阳能电池板的价格可能是传统设备的三到3.5倍，而传统设备通常由单层硅制成。 The cost of buying and installing conventional panels for solar farms ranges from about 93 cents to $1.06 per watt, according to a report by the Solar Energy Industries Association. 根据太阳能产业协会的一份报告，为太阳能发电场购买和安装传统太阳能电池板的成本约为每瓦93美分到1.06美元。 Andrés Gluski, chief executive of AES, a big utility and power company, said price would be crucial to the success of tandem panels because Chinese manufacturers sold solar panels at very low prices. China “could probably supply the world twice over,” he said. 大型公用事业和电力公司AES的首席执行官安德烈斯·格卢斯基表示，价格对叠层太阳能电池板的成功至关重要，因为中国制造商以极低价格销售太阳能电池板。他说，中国“可能足以满足全球两倍的需求”。 The technology for modern solar panels was created at AT&T’s Bell Labs in 1954. But broad use of it didn’t take off until the 1980s as the devices became more efficient at converting sunshine into electricity. Improvements helped lower costs and have made the technology the cheapest way to generate electricity. 现代太阳能板技术于1954年在AT&T的贝尔实验室诞生。但直到20世纪80年代，随着太阳能设备将阳光转化为电能的效率提高，该技术才开始得到广泛应用。技术的改进有助于降低成本，并使该技术成为最经济的发电方式。 In recent years, energy companies have also figured out how to pair solar panels with batteries to supply energy hours after the sun has set. Solar and batteries accounted for 70 percent of the capacity added to U.S. grids in the first half of this year, according to Wood Mackenzie, an energy research firm. 近年来，能源公司还摸索出了将太阳能电池板与电池相结合的方法，以便在日落后数小时仍能供电。根据能源研究公司伍德麦肯兹的数据，今年上半年，太阳能和电池占美国电网新增容量的70%。 Solar energy made up nearly 9 percent of the electricity produced in the United States in 2025, up from 3 percent in 2020, according to the Energy Information Administration. 根据美国能源信息署的数据，2025年太阳能占美国发电量的近9%，高于2020年的3%。 Widespread use of tandem panels could significantly increase solar’s share of the country’s electricity, helping to satisfy the surging demand for power from data centers used to develop artificial intelligence. 叠层太阳能板的广泛使用有望显著提高太阳能在美国电力中的份额，帮助满足用于开发人工智能的数据中心激增的电力需求。 Energy analysts evaluate the dependability of different sources of power by measuring their capacity factors. In theory, a power source that can supply electricity 24 hours a day, 365 days a year would have a capacity factor of 100 percent. But no power plants operate at that level because they require maintenance, upgrades, refueling and so on. 能源分析师通过衡量容量系数来评估不同电源的可靠性。理论上，一种能够一年365天、每天24小时供电的电源，其容量系数应为100%。但没有电厂能达到这一水平，因为它们需要进行维护、升级、补给燃料等操作。 Nuclear plants typically offer the highest capacity factors, in the low 90s. Large natural gas power plants generally operate at about 58 percent, while U.S. solar farms average roughly 24 percent, according to the E.I.A. That is primarily because they produce electricity only when the sun is shining and cannot convert all of the light they receive into usable energy. 核电站通常具有最高的容量系数，达到90%出头。根据美国能源信息署的数据，大型天然气发电厂一般以约58%的系数运行，而美国太阳能发电场的平均容量系数约为24%。这主要是因为它们只在阳光充足时发电，并且无法将接收到的所有光都转化为可用能源。 在Qcells的一个测试基地，羊群在太阳能电池板阵列间吃草。 Solar executives assert that tandem panels could have capacity factors of more than 31 percent. As a result, energy companies would be able to generate the same electricity on less land and with fewer materials. 太阳能行业高管坚称，叠层太阳能电池板的容量系数可能超过31%。因此，能源公司将能够在更少的土地上、使用更少的材料产生同样的电力。 The design of tandem panels favors First Solar, one of the few U.S. manufacturers that survived as Chinese producers became dominant. First Solar’s products use a thin film material that other manufactures would most likely need to perfect to make the layers in tandem panels. 叠层太阳能电池板的设计对First Solar很有利，它是在中国生产商占据主导地位时幸存下来的少数美国制造商之一。First Solar的产品使用一种薄膜材料，其他制造商若要制造叠层电池板中的各层，很可能需要先将这种材料完善。 “We’ve invested over $2 billion in thin film research and development, including this program,” said Mark Widmar, chief executive of First Solar, in Phoenix. “我们已在薄膜研发上投资超过20亿美元，包括这个项目，”位于凤凰城的First Solar 首席执行官马克·维德马说。 Some energy companies have bought early versions of the tandem panels to ensure that they do not get left behind, said Wayne Li, a principal at the Electric Power Research Institute, a nonprofit research organization. How dependable and durable the panels are will require extensive third-party testing, he added. 非营利研究机构电力研究院的负责人韦恩·李（音）说，一些能源公司已经购买了叠层太阳能电池板的早期版本，以确保自己不被时代淘汰。他还说，这些电池板的可靠性和耐用性还需要经过广泛的第三方测试。 “Manufacturers are not very open to share the details and the data,” Mr. Li said. “制造商不太愿意分享细节和数据，”韦恩·李说。 图片：Patrick Junker Ivan Penn是一名报道能源行业的记者，常驻洛杉矶。他的工作包括报道清洁能源、电网故障和公用事业的经济运作机制。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site
content: IVAN PENN 2026年10月13日 Producers of solar panels in the United States say they are on the cusp of a technological breakthrough that could upend the industry and even threaten China’s grip on it. 美国太阳能板生产商表示，他们即将迎来一项技术突破，这项突破可能颠覆整个行业，甚至威胁到中国在该行业的垄断地位。 The manufacturers are racing to develop new kinds of panels that can generate 25 percent more energy than most such devices available today. If they are successful, the advance will allow the world to meet the rapidly rising demand for electricity with less land and roof area. 这些制造商正在竞相开发新型太阳能板，其发电量比目前市面上大多数同类产品高出25%。如果成功，这一进步将使世界能以更少的土地和屋顶面积来满足迅速增长的电力需求。 The new technology, known as tandem solar, involves adding second and third layers of material, like a layer cake, to allow panels to convert more of the sun’s radiance into electricity. 这项新技术被称为叠层太阳能，通过像层层蛋糕一样添加第二层和第三层材料，使太阳能电池板能够将更多的太阳辐射转化为电能。 Researchers have been working to perfect tandem panels for many years, but now several companies, including Tandem PV, First Solar and Hanwha Qcells, say they are preparing to sell such panels commercially soon, after successfully testing the devices and obtaining certifications from technical bodies. 研究人员多年来一直致力于完善叠层太阳能电池板，但现在，包括Tandem PV、First Solar和韩华Qcells在内的几家公司表示，在成功测试这些设备并获得技术机构认证后，他们正准备很快将此类电池板投入商业销售。 “It is the next frontier,” said Mike Carr, executive director of the Solar Energy Manufacturers for America Coalition. He acknowledged that Chinese companies were also working on tandem solar but said their technology “is not better than ours and maybe even behind us.” “这是下一个前沿领域，”美国太阳能制造商联盟执行主任迈克·卡尔说。他承认中国企业也在研发叠层太阳能，但表示中国的技术“不比我们的更好，甚至可能落后于我们”。 But the new tandem panels and their manufacturers will face many challenges. Power producers will be reluctant to buy new devices that are too expensive or until manufacturers can convince them that tandem panels will not degrade more quickly than conventional panels. 但新的叠层太阳能板及其制造商将面临许多挑战。电力生产商将不愿购买过于昂贵的新设备，除非制造商能让他们相信，叠层太阳能电池的性能衰减速度不会比传统太阳能电池更快。 U.S. politics could be another barrier. Republicans in Congress and the Trump administration have made it hard for new solar farms to obtain federal permits while trying to increase the use of fossil fuels and nuclear power plants. 美国政治可能是另一个障碍。国会共和党人和特朗普政府一方面试图增加化石燃料和核电站的使用，一方面让新的太阳能发电场难以获得联邦许可。 Then there is China, which controls about 80 percent of the solar panel market by supplying either panels or their components. 此外还有中国，它通过供应太阳能板及其组件控制着约80%的太阳能板市场。 China devastated the U.S. solar panel manufacturing industry by offering devices at prices far lower than companies in the United States, Germany and Japan — which dominated the industry until around 2010. 中国以远低于美国、德国和日本公司的价格提供设备，重创了美国太阳能板制造业；此前，美国、德国和日本曾主导该行业直至2010年左右。 The Biden and Trump administrations have tried to revive U.S. solar manufacturing with tariffs, subsidies and other policies. Partly as a result, new factories have been built across the country in recent years. Hanwha, a South Korean company that bought the German solar manufacturer Qcells in 2012, has spent billions on production lines in Georgia, including in Cartersville, north of Atlanta. 拜登和特朗普政府都试图通过关税、补贴和其他政策重振美国太阳能制造业。部分得益于此，近年来美国各地纷纷建起了新工厂。韩国企业韩华在2012年收购了德国太阳能制造商 Qcells，已在佐治亚州的生产线上投入数十亿美元，包括亚特兰大以北的卡特斯维尔。 Energy experts say perfecting tandem panels before the Chinese do would allow the United States, Germany and other countries to reclaim a big share of the global solar industry. 能源专家表示，若能在中国之前完善叠层电池技术，美国、德国及其他国家将有望重新夺回全球太阳能产业的巨大份额。 Qcells has been testing its tandem solar panels in its lab in Germany as well as in fields in the United States, Australia, Cyprus and South Korea to show that they are ready. Among other things, the company has been blasting panels with LED light to see how they will perform. It has also been firing balls of ice — some roughly the size of marbles, others as big as or slightly bigger than golf balls — at panels to see how they handle extreme weather. Qcells一直在其德国实验室以及美国、澳大利亚、塞浦路斯和韩国的实地测试其叠层太阳能电池板，以证明它们已经准备就绪。除其他测试外，该公司一直用 LED 光照射太阳能电池板，以观察其表现。它还向太阳能电池板发射冰丸——有些大约弹珠大小，另一些与高尔夫球一样大或略大——以检验其应对极端天气的能力。。 Qcells公司进行的一项测试中模拟了冰雹。 The tests are designed to reassure energy companies, investors and lenders that the new panels will last 20 to 30 years once they are installed in baking deserts or in fields subject to torrential downpours. 这些测试旨在让能源公司、投资者和贷款方放心：无论安装在酷热的沙漠中，还是在常受暴雨侵袭的田野里，这些新的太阳能电池板都能使用20至30年。 The power industry is “quite conservative in accepting new technologies,” said Fabian Fertig, head of tandem research and development for Qcells, who is based in Leipzig, Germany. “We’ve been focused on stability. We have to convince banks that this new technology can deliver.” 电力行业“在接受新技术方面相当保守”，Qcells叠层研发负责人法比安·费尔蒂希说。他常驻德国莱比锡。“我们一直专注于稳定性。我们必须让银行相信，这项新技术能够兑现承诺。” Scientists developed early tandem panels decades ago, but it has taken time to ensure that they could withstand harsh conditions — from heat and humidity to pounding hail. 科学家早在几十年前就开发出了早期叠层太阳能电池板，但要确保它们能够承受从高温、高湿到猛烈冰雹等各种恶劣条件，仍花费了相当长的时间。 “There are all these questions around how long they actually last,” said Chetan Krishna, a principal at RMI, a research organization that specializes in sustainability and was previously known as the Rocky Mountain Institute. “Are there degradation issues that we don’t know yet?” “围绕它们实际能用多久存在各种各样的问题，”RMI（一家专注于可持续发展的研究机构，前身为落基山研究所）负责人切坦·克里希纳说。“是否存在我们尚不知道的衰减问题？” Mr. Krishna and other experts say they believe the tandem solar panels are very close to being ready. 克里希纳和其他专家表示，他们认为叠层太阳能电池板已非常接近投入实际应用。 But the technology remains expensive. By some estimates, these panels could cost three to three and a half times as much as conventional devices, which are typically made of one layer of silicon. 但这项技术仍然昂贵。根据一些估计，这些太阳能电池板的价格可能是传统设备的三到3.5倍，而传统设备通常由单层硅制成。 The cost of buying and installing conventional panels for solar farms ranges from about 93 cents to $1.06 per watt, according to a report by the Solar Energy Industries Association. 根据太阳能产业协会的一份报告，为太阳能发电场购买和安装传统太阳能电池板的成本约为每瓦93美分到1.06美元。 Andrés Gluski, chief executive of AES, a big utility and power company, said price would be crucial to the success of tandem panels because Chinese manufacturers sold solar panels at very low prices. China “could probably supply the world twice over,” he said. 大型公用事业和电力公司AES的首席执行官安德烈斯·格卢斯基表示，价格对叠层太阳能电池板的成功至关重要，因为中国制造商以极低价格销售太阳能电池板。他说，中国“可能足以满足全球两倍的需求”。 The technology for modern solar panels was created at AT&T’s Bell Labs in 1954. But broad use of it didn’t take off until the 1980s as the devices became more efficient at converting sunshine into electricity. Improvements helped lower costs and have made the technology the cheapest way to generate electricity. 现代太阳能板技术于1954年在AT&T的贝尔实验室诞生。但直到20世纪80年代，随着太阳能设备将阳光转化为电能的效率提高，该技术才开始得到广泛应用。技术的改进有助于降低成本，并使该技术成为最经济的发电方式。 In recent years, energy companies have also figured out how to pair solar panels with batteries to supply energy hours after the sun has set. Solar and batteries accounted for 70 percent of the capacity added to U.S. grids in the first half of this year, according to Wood Mackenzie , an energy research firm. 近年来，能源公司还摸索出了将太阳能电池板与电池相结合的方法，以便在日落后数小时仍能供电。 根据能源研究公司伍德麦肯兹的数据 ，今年上半年，太阳能和电池占美国电网新增容量的70%。 Solar energy made up nearly 9 percent of the electricity produced in the United States in 2025, up from 3 percent in 2020, according to the Energy Information Administration. 根据美国能源信息署的数据，2025年太阳能占美国发电量的近9%，高于2020年的3%。 Widespread use of tandem panels could significantly increase solar’s share of the country’s electricity, helping to satisfy the surging demand for power from data centers used to develop artificial intelligence. 叠层太阳能板的广泛使用有望显著提高太阳能在美国电力中的份额，帮助满足用于开发人工智能的数据中心激增的电力需求。 Energy analysts evaluate the dependability of different sources of power by measuring their capacity factors. In theory, a power source that can supply electricity 24 hours a day, 365 days a year would have a capacity factor of 100 percent. But no power plants operate at that level because they require maintenance, upgrades, refueling and so on. 能源分析师通过衡量容量系数来评估不同电源的可靠性。理论上，一种能够一年365天、每天24小时供电的电源，其容量系数应为100%。但没有电厂能达到这一水平，因为它们需要进行维护、升级、补给燃料等操作。 Nuclear plants typically offer the highest capacity factors, in the low 90s. Large natural gas power plants generally operate at about 58 percent, while U.S. solar farms average roughly 24 percent, according to the E.I.A. That is primarily because they produce electricity only when the sun is shining and cannot convert all of the light they receive into usable energy. 核电站通常具有最高的容量系数，达到90%出头。根据美国能源信息署的数据，大型天然气发电厂一般以约58%的系数运行，而美国太阳能发电场的平均容量系数约为24%。这主要是因为它们只在阳光充足时发电，并且无法将接收到的所有光都转化为可用能源。 在Qcells的一个测试基地，羊群在太阳能电池板阵列间吃草。 Solar executives assert that tandem panels could have capacity factors of more than 31 percent. As a result, energy companies would be able to generate the same electricity on less land and with fewer materials. 太阳能行业高管坚称，叠层太阳能电池板的容量系数可能超过31%。因此，能源公司将能够在更少的土地上、使用更少的材料产生同样的电力。 The design of tandem panels favors First Solar, one of the few U.S. manufacturers that survived as Chinese producers became dominant. First Solar’s products use a thin film material that other manufactures would most likely need to perfect to make the layers in tandem panels. 叠层太阳能电池板的设计对First Solar很有利，它是在中国生产商占据主导地位时幸存下来的少数美国制造商之一。First Solar的产品使用一种薄膜材料，其他制造商若要制造叠层电池板中的各层，很可能需要先将这种材料完善。 “We’ve invested over $2 billion in thin film research and development, including this program,” said Mark Widmar, chief executive of First Solar, in Phoenix. “我们已在薄膜研发上投资超过20亿美元，包括这个项目，”位于凤凰城的First Solar 首席执行官马克·维德马说。 Some energy companies have bought early versions of the tandem panels to ensure that they do not get left behind, said Wayne Li, a principal at the Electric Power Research Institute, a nonprofit research organization. How dependable and durable the panels are will require extensive third-party testing, he added. 非营利研究机构电力研究院的负责人韦恩·李（音）说，一些能源公司已经购买了叠层太阳能电池板的早期版本，以确保自己不被时代淘汰。他还说，这些电池板的可靠性和耐用性还需要经过广泛的第三方测试。 “Manufacturers are not very open to share the details and the data,” Mr. Li said. “制造商不太愿意分享细节和数据，”韦恩·李说。 图片：Patrick Junker Ivan Penn 是一名报道能源行业的记者，常驻洛杉矶。他的工作包括报道清洁能源、电网故障和公用事业的经济运作机制。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

title: “草木皆兵”：一个更富裕强大的中国在害怕什么？
description: ANDREW HIGGINS2026年10月12日今年1月，时报记者安德鲁·希金斯乘车经过天安门广场。1989年6月，他曾亲历军队对抗议腐败、不平等和通货膨胀的民众展开武力镇压的现场。 It was an enjoyable day of temple and factory visits organized by China Daily, the Communist Party’s English-language mouthpiece, but it ended on an uncomfortable note. 那是中共官方英文媒体《中国日报》组织的一次令人愉快的寺庙与工厂探访之旅，结尾却令人颇感不适。 The group I was traveling with in the northern province of Shanxi — mostly foreign influencers hungry for followers and Chinese freebies — was told to line up behind a long banner and be filmed chanting: “Amazing China, Amazing Shanxi.” 与我一同前往北方省份山西的这群人主要是渴望粉丝和免费福利的外国网红，他们被要求在一条长横幅后排开，并对着镜头合唱：“Amazing China, Amazing Shanxi”（大美中国，大美山西）。 I declined to join in, scowling in silence. But, back in my hotel room in the provincial capital of Taiyuan, I felt I had perhaps been too churlish: Getting a bunch of foreigners to chant on cue for the camera about China’s wonders was a transparent but harmless propaganda stunt. 我拒绝配合，面带不悦地冷眼旁观。不过，回到省会太原的酒店房间后，我又觉得自己的态度或许过于生硬了：让一群外国人对着镜头按指令合唱对中国奇迹的赞歌，不过是个显而易见却也无害的宣传把戏而已。 And, to be honest, the 11th century temples we visited — and also the new highway that took us to them — were pretty amazing. 况且说实话，我们参观的11世纪古刹——以及把我们送到那里的新建高速公路——确实相当惊人。 Then I received a message on WeChat, a Chinese messaging app, from an old friend in Beijing, a lawyer whose earnest decency and movie star looks always reminded me of the “good party cadre” characters in propaganda films. I had not seen him for more than 30 years and was planning to visit the following day. 随后，我的微信收到了一条来自北京一位老朋友的信息。他是一名律师，为人真诚得体，长相如明星般英俊，总让我想起宣传电影里那些“优秀党员干部”形象。我已有30多年没见过他，本计划第二天去拜访他。 Sadly, his message said, he would not be able to keep our appointment because state security officers, somehow apprised of our plans, had turned up at his door and ordered him to cancel. 遗憾的是，他在信息中说自己无法赴约了，因为国家安全官员不知通过什么渠道获悉了我们的行程，直接找上了他的家门，命令他取消见面的计划。 China suddenly appeared not so much amazing as alarming. 一瞬间，中国带给我的不再是惊艳，而是惊恐。 After decades away from the country where I studied classical Chinese in 1980-81 and then worked as a journalist from 1987 until 1991, I returned in September last year for a six-month assignment. I marveled at how much had changed, sharing the amazement of first-time visitors awe-struck by China’s high-speed trains, dazzling modern cities and gung-ho embrace of the future. 我曾于1980至1981年间在中国学习古汉语，后于1987年至1991年担任驻华记者。在离开这个国家数十年后，我于去年9月返回中国执行为期六个月的报道任务。我惊叹于这里的巨变，和那些初次踏足这片土地的游客一样，我被中国的高铁网络、耀眼的现代都市以及对未来的热切拥抱所震撼。 1981年，戴着围巾的希金斯在山东大学食堂。当时，食堂只供应油乎乎的粥和馒头，粥里漂着几块不知是什么的肉。 My old friend’s message broke the reverie: 然而，我这位老友发来的消息打碎了这份美好： “Every bush and tree seems like an enemy soldier,” he warned, using a Chinese idiom to describe the paranoia of a security apparatus that has also changed dramatically. It has grown bigger, more intrusive and, thanks to high-tech marvels like WeChat and omnipresent surveillance cameras, much more capable of monitoring just about everyone. “草木皆兵，”他用这句中国成语提醒我，道出了如今安全机器的极度疑神疑鬼——这套机构自身同样经历了剧烈变化。它现在规模更大、侵入性更强；借助微信及无处不在的监控摄像头等高科技手段，它具备了对几乎所有人实施全天候监控的能力。 China’s economic transformation over the last four decades has been extraordinary, and it infuriates Chinese officials that Western media outlets display what they see as “anti-China bias.” That is shorthand for reporting that dwells on anxiety about the economy, still growing but at a slower pace, and anything else that deviates from China’s undeniable achievements and charms. 过去40年来，中国的经济转型无疑是卓越的，而西方媒体展现出的所谓“反华偏见“令中国官员极为恼火。所谓“反华偏见“，指的是那些着重渲染中国经济焦虑的报道—​​—尽管中国经济仍在增长，但增速放缓——以及任何与中国无可否认的成就和魅力相悖的内容。 Throughout my stay, I struggled to reconcile the reality of a country that has never been richer and seemingly full of promise with a parallel reality of brittle insecurity, in which every bush and tree hides a potential enemy. 在华停留期间，我一直在试图调和这种撕裂感：一方面，这个国家从未如此富裕，似乎充满希望；另一方面，它又存在着一种脆弱的安全感缺失，仿佛每一株草木背后都潜伏着未知的敌人。 Based in Shanghai, I often went on weekends with my wife to a park in the city’s northern Hongkou district, where groups of older Chinese gather to sing songs from their youth. Their favorite numbers are patriotic anthems but the singers, who often included a Uyghur man dressed and made up to look like Charlie Chaplin, were there of their own accord. 在上海期间，我和妻子经常在周末前往该市北部的虹口公园。那里聚集着许多中老年人，他们自发凑在一起演唱年轻时代的歌曲。他们最爱唱的是爱国歌曲——经常能看到其中有一位装扮成查理·卓别林的维吾尔族男子——但完全是出于自愿参与其中。 Their boisterous camaraderie and national pride seemed entirely genuine. 他们欢聚的热烈氛围与国家自豪感看起来完全出自真心。 An official sign nearby, however, clouded the carefree mood: “Opposing Traitors and Guarding Against Spies Starts With Us,” it warned, with a phone number to “report espionage activity.” 然而，附近挂着的一块官方告示牌却为这种无忧无虑的氛围蒙上了阴影，牌子上警告道：“反间防谍，从我做起，”并附上了“举报间谍行为”的电话号码。 The hunt for spies has escalated sharply since Xi Jinping took power in 2012 and began throttling the flow of information in and out of China, building up the Great Firewall to prevent Chinese from viewing many foreign websites. 自习近平于2012年执政并开始收紧跨境信息流动、修筑防火长城以阻断国内民众访问众多外国网站以来，针对间谍行为的打击急剧升级。 There are seemingly no limits on what the state can see and hear, and ordinary Chinese have adapted accordingly — most noticeably with regard to the leader himself. 国家的监控范围似乎辽阔无边，普通民众也相应地作出了调适——最明显的莫过于对待最高领导人本人的态度。 北京一条繁华步行街上的摄像头。国家能够看到和听到什么似乎已不受任何限制。 Mr. Xi is everywhere, on television, on billboards and on the front pages of newspapers and websites. But, throughout my stay in China, not one of the hundreds of Chinese I spoke to, mostly in private, ever uttered his name out loud. Even foreigners often avoided it, pointing at the ceiling when they wanted to refer to China’s president. 习近平的身影无处不在，电视上、广告牌上、报纸和网站的头版上都有他。然而，在我停留中国期间私下接触的数百名中国人中，没有一个人敢大声念出他的名字。甚至连外国人也往往避开提及，当想指代中国国家主席时，他们只是用手指指天花板。 The Chinese people whom I met on my travels invariably skirted politics, except when I encountered a zealous patriot during a visit to Dazhai, a former Maoist model commune in a remote mountain area of Shanxi. “Which is better, China or America? Tell the truth!” he shouted, in between praise of China’s leadership and ridicule of the United States and Europe. 我在行程中接触到的中国人无一例外地避谈政治，只有一次例外：在访问山西偏远山区一处毛泽东时代示范公社大寨时，我遇到了一位狂热的爱国者。“到底是中国好还是美国好？说实话！”他在赞美中国领导层、嘲弄美欧之余，对我大声嚷嚷道。 Nobody voiced open political dissent but many grumbled about the economy, particularly in places like Hainan Island where a runaway property boom has ground to a halt. There is also a security check at the station, where guards, unfailingly polite, put all passengers’ bags through a scanner. Behind them was a cabinet stuffed with black batons, helmets and other riot control gear. Next to an ad for high-end dog food, a propaganda poster demanded vigilance against unspecified threats. 从我在苏州河畔闪亮的新建高楼里的公寓步行到最近的地铁站，短短一百多米的距离内，我数出了30多个正对着行人的摄像头。地铁站内还设有安检，态度极其礼貌的安检员要求所有乘客将包袋放进扫描仪。在他们身后，摆放着一个塞满黑色警棍、头盔和其他防暴装备的器材柜。一则高端狗粮广告的旁边贴着一张宣传海报，要求警惕未指明的安全威胁。 Vigilance against supposed spies in China has cursed foreign journalists looking for information, no matter how anodyne, for many decades. 对所谓间谍的高度警惕几十年来一直像咒语一样困扰着试图获取信息的外国记者，哪怕这些信息极其寻常。 When I worked there as a journalist in the 1980s, communism was crumbling next door in the Soviet Union and restlessness over corruption and one-party rule led to huge protests in Tiananmen Square. The food was excellent. 我们完全避开了过去谈话中常出现的政治小道消息。午餐的菜肴非常美味。 When I first went to China as a student, I lived in Jinan, an eastern center for state-owned heavy industry that reeked of coal.
